patterns: Judge.me repeats page 100 after the 10,000-row cap.
Every review count must name its population.
Body hash is the local syndication-dedup key.

novel_features.name: Completeness-safe mirror
novel_features.description: Mirror the complete review corpus and refuse success when unique IDs do not equal Judge.me's live count.
novel_features.rationale: The API silently repeats page 100 after 10,000 rows, so safe sync requires loop detection, partitioning, deduplication, and count assertions.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before any analysis that depends on corpus completeness.

novel_features.name: Filtered corpus export
novel_features.description: Export explicit published, hidden, pending, or all populations as JSON or CSV.
novel_features.rationale: A verified local mirror enables fast, repeatable filtering without another fragile full-API traversal.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to hand a bounded, provenance-labeled review slice to downstream analysis tools.

novel_features.name: Population census
novel_features.description: Count storefront-visible and internal moderation populations with unambiguous labels.
novel_features.rationale: Judge.me returns reviews the storefront does not show, so one raw total is operationally misleading.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this whenever published-vs-hidden population differences affect a report or decision.

novel_features.name: Syndication clusters
novel_features.description: Find identical normalized review bodies attached to multiple products.
novel_features.rationale: Body hashes in the local mirror expose bundle syndication that row-level API data obscures.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before attributing customer language to a specific SKU or product.

novel_features.name: Unique-body view
novel_features.description: Return one deterministic representative per normalized review body while retaining source row counts.
novel_features.rationale: Deduplicating by body hash prevents syndicated copies from dominating VoC analysis.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when independent customer voices matter more than API row count.

narrative.headline: A completeness-verified Judge.me review corpus with explicit populations and syndication-aware exports.
narrative.value_prop: Wrap the full Judge.me API while defending review workflows against the silent 10,000-row pagination loop. Sync once into a documented SQLite mirror, then export, count, and deduplicate published or internal review populations with provenance on every agent response.
narrative.auth_narrative: Set JUDGEME_API_KEY to the private token and JUDGEME_SHOP_DOMAIN to the store's myshopify.com domain. The private token is sent only in the X-Api-Token header and is redacted from logs; it is never placed in a request URL.

quickstart.comment: Build the verified local review mirror before analysis.
Confirm which population each count represents.

troubleshoots.symptom: Sync stops after detecting a repeated page.
troubleshoots.fix: Rerun `judgeme-pp-cli sync --resources reviews --full`; the safe paginator will partition and must match `/reviews/count` before committing.

troubleshoots.symptom: A report count is higher than the storefront count.
troubleshoots.fix: Pass `--population published`; the default `all` population includes reviews Judge.me does not show on the storefront.

troubleshoots.symptom: Product-level VoC contains identical language across bundle SKUs.
troubleshoots.fix: Run `judgeme-pp-cli reviews syndication --agent`, then use `judgeme-pp-cli reviews unique-bodies --population published`.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI for Judge.me review synchronization, moderation inspection, export, storefront-widget access, and syndication-aware customer-language analysis. Prefer the local review mirror when exact corpus completeness or repeatable filtering matters.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to infer which syndicated product association is the true one.
Do not use raw `reviews index` pagination as proof of full-corpus completeness.
Do not use mutation commands without reviewing the dry-run and passing the explicit apply flag.
